analysis: Examined base and head of provider-swift/Tests/DarkbloomCLITests/SandboxWorkDiskTests.swift. The only changes (head lines 197, 226, 246, 279, 304, 334, 375, 402, 426; range map complete) add a `waitlist: .approved` argument to every SandboxSetupFlow construction. Test assertions, the disk checks, the ownership-enable flow, the installer arguments and the request counts are otherwise unchanged. This is test-only code, so it adds no runtime attack surface. It does imply a new production SandboxSetupFlow parameter, which is outside this batch. That parameter is a waitlist gate on `darkbloom sandbox setup` (TB-013, A-019, T-061). Integration should check that production code: (1) defaults to a real waitlist check and not to approved, (2) does not let a sandbox-server waitlist response skip the installer integrity and confirmation path or add new execution or trust, (3) leaves the internal-disk fallback and ownership-enable sudo prompt unchanged, and (4) handles waitlist network data without leaking the owner's identity or tokens (A-008). Every test pins `.approved`, so the tests would not detect a waitlist bypass or a fail-open on network error; the production waitlist logic needs its own review. No regression is identifiable from this unit.
